sources.scope: MCP Server and API sections: catalog/selected outputs, configured file access and optional Node processing.
MCP workflow introduction and follow-up export/protocol updates.

previous_acceptance_test: Perform MCP initialize/list-tools/crawl/read/export using a local client; keep script execution an explicit capability.
expanded_acceptance_test: Perform the basic official-client workflow and cover discoverable reports/bulk exports/field-filter projections, stored content outputs, configured base-directory file tools and explicitly enabled Node/npm processing across supported transports; track each sub-contract separately.
remaining_acceptance: Expose and prove report, bulk-export, filter and data-field discovery with typed selected-field/format/segment/full-selection exports; existing snapshot and sitemap exports prove narrower contracts.

Implement configured base-directory text read/write, directory discovery/list/create and explicit disabled-by-default Node script/npm capabilities. Prove exact target containment, unsupported paths, defaults, output/error/deadline/actual child drain and retained outputs with independent fixtures.

Prove stored URL content/image/screenshot outputs, stable selected-crawl workflow and same source/config/error behavior using real official SDK clients on both transports. The static26-tool registry and historical11-tool basic workflow are not full reference MCP coverage.
qualification: Source inspection and public-reference scope audit only. Absence from the closed26-tool inventory proves these typed MCP entry points are not exposed here; it does not prove runtime behavior or vendor algorithm equivalence. Historical narrower successful workflows and immutable source/publication receipts remain valid within their recorded scope.
